solution: First line \(\frac{x}{3}=\frac{y}{4}=z\) has direction ratios \((3,4,1)\); second line has d.r. \((k,3,k-1)\). Perpendicular \(\Rightarrow\) dot \(=0\): \(3k+12+(k-1)=0\Rightarrow 4k+11=0\Rightarrow k=-\frac{11}{4}\).

Write \(2x-1=3y+2=z-2=t\). Then \(x=\frac{t+1}{2}\Rightarrow x-\frac12=\frac{t}{2}\), \(y=\frac{t-2}{3}\Rightarrow y+\frac23=\frac{t}{3}\), \(z-2=t\). Symmetric form \(\frac{x-1/2}{1/2}=\frac{y+2/3}{1/3}=\frac{z-2}{1}\); scaling d.r. by 6 gives \((3,2,6)\), point \(\left(\frac12,-\frac23,2\right)\). So \(\bar{r}=\left(\frac12\hat{i}-\frac23\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right)+\lambda(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+6\hat{k})\).

Point on line \(A=(0,1,2)\), d.r. \(\bar{b}=(1,2,3)\), \(P=(1,6,3)\), \(\overline{AP}=(1,5,1)\). \(\overline{AP}\times\bar{b}=(5\cdot3-1\cdot2,\,-(1\cdot3-1\cdot1),\,1\cdot2-5\cdot1)=(13,-2,-3)\). Distance \(=\frac{|\overline{AP}\times\bar{b}|}{|\bar{b}|}=\frac{\sqrt{169+4+9}}{\sqrt{14}}=\frac{\sqrt{182}}{\sqrt{14}}=\sqrt{13}\).

**[MISMATCH: computed value \(\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\approx0.98\) matches no option]** \(\bar{a_1}=(1,2,1),\bar{b_1}=(1,-1,-1),\bar{a_2}=(2,-1,-1),\bar{b_2}=(2,1,2)\). \(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=(-1,-4,3)\), \(|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|=\sqrt{26}\). \(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=(1,-3,-2)\); dot \(=(1)(-1)+(-3)(-4)+(-2)(3)=5\). Shortest distance \(=\frac{|5|}{\sqrt{26}}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\approx0.98\), which equals none of the options (\(\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\approx0.58,\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\approx0.71,\frac{3}{\sqrt2}\approx2.12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\approx0.87\)). Closest is \(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\) (D). Likely book defect.

Line1: \((t,2t,3t)\) d.r. \((1,2,3)\); Line2 point \((1,2,3)\) d.r. \((-2,-4,6)\). d.r. not proportional (\(-2,-4,6\) vs \(1,2,3\)), so not parallel/coincident; dot \(=1(-2)+2(-4)+3(6)=8\neq0\), not perpendicular. Solving \((t,2t,3t)=(1-2s,2-4s,3+6s)\): \(t=1-2s\) and \(3t=3+6s\Rightarrow t=1+2s\Rightarrow s=0,t=1\), consistent with middle eqn. They meet at \((1,2,3)\): intersecting.
The X-axis consists of all points \((x,0,0)\); i.e. \(y=0,\ z=0\).

Line1 \(2x=3y=-z=t\Rightarrow\) d.r. \(\left(\frac12,\frac13,-1\right)\propto(3,2,-6)\). Line2 \(6x=-y=-4z=t\Rightarrow\) d.r. \(\left(\frac16,-1,-\frac14\right)\propto(2,-12,-3)\). Dot \(=3(2)+2(-12)+(-6)(-3)=6-24+18=0\Rightarrow\) angle \(=90^\circ\).
Distance of \(2x+3y-z=k\) from origin \(=\frac{|k|}{\sqrt{2^2+3^2+(-1)^2}}=\frac{|k|}{\sqrt{14}}=\sqrt{14}\Rightarrow|k|=14\). Option gives \(k=14\).

Parallel planes \(\Rightarrow\) normals proportional: \((2,-\lambda,1)\parallel(4,-1,\mu)\). \(\frac{2}{4}=\frac12=c\); \(-1=c(-\lambda)=-2\lambda\Rightarrow\lambda=\frac12\); \(\mu=c(1)\cdot2\)... using \(4=2\cdot2\): scale \(c=2\), so \(\mu=2\cdot1=2\), \(\lambda=\frac12\). Thus \(\left(\frac12,2\right)\).
Equal intercepts: \(\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{a}+\frac{z}{a}=1\Rightarrow x+y+z=a\). Through \((2,-1,3)\): \(a=2-1+3=4\). Plane \(x+y+z=4\).
Normals \((5,-2,3)\) and \((15,-6,9)=3(5,-2,3)\) are parallel, so the planes are parallel; angle between them \(=0^\circ\).
Normal \(\bar{n}=(2,-1,2)\), \(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3\). Direction cosines \(=\left(\frac23,-\frac13,\frac23\right)\).

Parallel to Y-axis \(\Rightarrow\) normal has zero \(j\)-component: plane \(ax+cz=d\). Through \((1,-1,1)\): \(a+c=d\); through \((3,2,4)\): \(3a+4c=d\). Subtract: \(2a+3c=0\Rightarrow a=-\frac{3c}{2}\); take \(c=2,a=-3,d=-1\): \(-3x+2z=-1\Rightarrow 3x-2z=1\). Check: \((1,-1,1)\to3-2=1\), \((3,2,4)\to9-8=1\).

Normal \(=\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\), \(\bar{b_1}=(4,4,-5),\bar{b_2}=(7,1,3)\): \(i:4(3)-(-5)(1)=17\); \(j:-(4(3)-(-5)(7))=-47\); \(k:4(1)-4(7)=-24\). Plane through \((5,7,-3)\): \(17(x-5)-47(y-7)-24(z+3)=0\Rightarrow17x-47y-24z+172=0\). (Note: substituting the second line's point \((8,4,-5)\) gives \(240\neq0\), i.e. \((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=240\neq0\), so the two given lines are actually skew, not coplanar — a mild book defect; option A is the plane determined by line 1 and the common normal.)
d.r. \((2,3,6)\cdot\) normal \((3,-14,6)=6-42+36=0\) (line \(\parallel\) plane). Point \((-1,m,4)\) must lie on plane: \(3(-1)-14m+6(4)+49=0\Rightarrow70-14m=0\Rightarrow m=5\).
Foot of perpendicular from origin \((4,-2,-5)\) is the direction of the normal and a point on the plane. Plane \(4x-2y-5z=d\) with \(d=4(4)-2(-2)-5(-5)=16+4+25=45\). Plane: \(4x-2y-5z=45\).
